### Release 9, Slice 1 design (2026-10-29)

Designed in the Slice 1 design proposal from three read-only surveys of `main` at `cfcc9a6c7` (the send
path and QoS vocabulary; scheduling, timers and bounded collections; typed channels, consumers, the conformance
lane and the harness); the decisions are D465 to D474, under the maintainer's rulings R1–R5 of 2026-10-29, each
taken on its recommended option. The proposal is deleted with S1-ii's close: its §1–§6 are in git history at
`86800bff2` (#734), and its §7, S1-ii's design, is D476–D482 here. Slice 1 lands as two pull requests (R4):
S1-i, the paced lane, and S1-ii, its bounds, fairness, consumer proof and hosted placement. R6 approved the S1-i
plan as written, and R7 gave retention and the cadence shared owners (D475).

- **The home (D465, R1).** Pacing is a stage in the ALM outbound lifecycle before per-envelope admission; a staged
  value keeps the identity and deadline minted at construction and enters today's carrier admission unchanged.
- **The channel and the send (D466, D467, R2).** `purpose: 'live'` declares a required `publication` policy with no
  product default for any field; its sends are best-effort, unreceipted, volatile and 1 s, each names the
  `resourceId` of its stream and is conflated latest-wins on the stream key.
- **The state (D468).** A live send reads `staged` first; a displaced value settles `superseded`, a value whose
  deadline passes staged `expired`, and a value heavier than the drain budget is refused `oversized`.
- **Pacing (D469, D470, R5).** One lane per channel, the newest N values per stream, a drain budget per opportunity
  and no catch-up burst after a late wake, on one task of the session's queue engine with `wakeAt` and the injected
  epoch clock.
- **The wiring and the proof (D471–D474, R3).** The browser dispatch stages a live delivery on its connect's stage;
  the harness `messages.send` gains `purpose` and `publication`; three smoke cells over the three carriers, withheld
  from the hosted manifests until S1-ii placed them in manifest 18. No game feed moves in Slice 1 (R3).
- **Shared primitives (D475, R7).** `retainNewest` in `packages/shared/cache` and the cadence functions in
  `packages/shared/resilience`, shared with Rallar Motion's buffer and send gate.

S1-ii was designed on 2026-10-29 after #734 merged, from two read-only surveys of `main` at `86800bff2` (the WS
server's path for client room sends and the NACK channel; the ledger pattern, the metrics surfaces and the stage as
landed; the Recipe Console flows, the examples and the hosted manifests); the decisions are D476 to D482, under the
maintainer's rulings R8–R13 of 2026-10-29, each taken on its recommended option, and R14 approved the seven-task
plan as written.

- **The shared key stays (D476, R8).** A stream's values keep its latest-wins key; the drain budget bounds work per
  opportunity and promises no delivered history, so the cells assert the stage's selection.
- **Bounds (D477, R9).** One ledger per session's stage counts streams, staged values and staged bytes across its
  lanes (64 / 1 000 / 4 MiB) after retention, and refuses a value that would pass a limit `capacity` naming it.
- **Fairness, cancellation, reconfiguration (D478, D479, R10).** A per-lane cursor starts each opportunity at the
  stream after the last one served; lanes stay independent. A cancel settles a staged value `cancelled` on the
  stage before any carrier, and a changed policy re-trims, refuses the oversized and moves the next boundary
  earlier, never later.
- **The visible flow and the metrics (D480, R11).** A payload-free `publication-staging` diagnostic per value's
  outcome; `readUsage().publication` and `stats.rallar.alm.publication`; the Recipe Console's Analyze view shows a
  paced cell's rows, pinned by `recipe-console-publication.spec.ts`; `examples/room-live-channel/README.md` is the
  example, linked from the examples index and the example map.
- **The cells and hosted placement (D481, R12).** `paced-capacity`, `paced-fairness`, `paced-cancel`,
  `paced-isolation-resources` and `paced-isolation-lists` beside the S1-i cells at a 2 000 ms cadence, over the
  three carriers; manifest 18 carries the seven two-agent paced cells, and `paced-isolation-lists` is withheld
  from 22. One isolation cell separates two resources of one channel and the other two fixed recipients; two
  groups are two streams by the stream key, which S1-i pins on the key, with no cell of their own.
- **The WS live-only refusal (D482, R13).** The WS server refuses a volatile best-effort latest-wins publication on
  a topic whose effective fanout is `outbox` at ingress, `unsupported` and terminal, and never enqueues it.

### Release 9, Slice 2 design (2026-10-29)

Designed in the Slice 2 design proposal from four read-only surveys of `main` at `cc629d767`
(group-state governance and persistence; WS topics, admission and audience; the browser surface and the
conformance harness; api-v1 routes, OpenAPI and black-box recipes); the decisions are D483 to D501, under the
maintainer's rulings S2-R1–S2-R10 of 2026-10-29, each taken on its recommended option. D492–D501 are design choices
made under the rulings, D499 ruled by the maintainer as S2-R10. Slice 2 lands as two pull requests (D483): S2-i,
publication grants and their enforcement on every WS path, and S2-ii, session subscriptions, the audience
intersection, the browser topic roles and the four-role proof. S2-R11 approved the seven-task S2-i plan as written.
The proposal is deleted with S2-ii's close: it is in git history at `4146e42ee` (#744), and S2-ii's design under
the maintainer's rulings S2ii-R1–S2ii-R5 is D502–D511 here. S2ii-R4 approved the six-task S2-ii plan as written.

- **The grant store and its lifetime (D484, D485, S2-R2, S2-R3).** One row per principal in
  `group-state:publication-grants`, exact topics with `publish` and `subscribe`, at most 64 (D495's `capacity`). A
  grant write compares-and-sets the group row and bumps `snapshotVersion` only, so nothing replans; a departure
  deletes the row in its own batch, retirement deletes it, and a non-active group holds no effective grant.
- **The commands (D492–D494).** `grantGroupPublication` and `revokeGroupPublication` through AppInbox, with REST,
  OpenAPI and the two recipes; grant adds and revoke removes the named permissions, a change-less command is a
  `no-op`, an owner may grant itself and an admin governs regular members only. The creator's declared grant rides
  `CreateGroupRequest.publicationGrants`.
- **Exposure (D488, D501).** `publicationGrants` on `GroupSnapshot` and its delta, the `publication-grant-changed`
  event, and one effective reader, `resolveGroupPublicationPermissions`, that never lets a spectator or a non-active
  member publish.
- **Enforcement (D486, D487, D496–D499).** A WS topic declares `participation: 'members' | 'granted'`; on a granted
  topic `computeRoomPublicationAdmission` admits a session holding `publish` or a listed server producer and reaches
  the sessions of principals holding `subscribe`, on every pass, for proxies on the original sender's grant, and
  again at every dispatch step through the re-check port. A refusal is `no-publish-grant`, `topic-not-granted` or
  `unsupported`; the receipt keeps a revoked recipient expected and unconfirmed. api-v1 installs its granted topics
  from `grantedWsTopics`.
- **The browser (D491, D500).** A typed channel declares `access`; a granted channel refuses a send its cached
  snapshot grants no `publish` before any carrier, and which of its sends ride RTC is Slice 3's (D512–D523).

- **The subscription store and its lifetime (D489, D502–D504, S2ii-R1, S2ii-R2).** One row per (group, session,
  topic) in `group-state:subscriptions`, naming the asserting connection generation, the lease's end and the
  admitting group revision; the 120 s lease is the store expiry. The write is the row alone, guarded by itself: no
  event, revision or delta. A revoke of `subscribe` and every departure delete the rows in the same write; a grant
  that adds `subscribe` and an activation delete a racing orphan; retirement deletes them.
- **The commands (D502, D503, D507).** `subscribeGroupTopic` and `unsubscribeGroupTopic` through AppInbox, with the
  self-session REST pair under `.../sessions/{sessionId}/`, the session's subscription list, OpenAPI and the
  `api-v1-group-topic-subscriptions` recipe. Outcomes `subscribed`, `renewed`, `unsubscribed` and `not-subscribed`;
  refusals `no-subscribe-grant`, `stale-generation` and `no-live-session`; the generation is matched as a value
  against the session's live client-state rows.
- **Authority and intersection (D508).** A fresh server-only read of the topic's rows and the sessions' live
  generations beside the probed snapshot; the audience is live active-member sessions holding `subscribe` with a
  live-asserted leased row, intersected with targeting and the leader, on every WS path; the captured generations
  are compared at every dispatch step, and an empty audience is admitted with zero recipients.
- **The browser (D490, D509).** `topicGrants`, `topicRole`, `grantTopic` and `revokeTopic` on the room facade; a
  granted channel's `subscribe(handler)` token, owned per tab, ref-counted per room and topic, renewed on the
  heartbeat cadence, re-asserted on reopen and released at session end.
- **The four-role family (D491, D505, D506, D510, D511).** `sender`, `publisher-b`, `receiver` and `sibling` over
  `ws` and `rtc-with-ws-fallback`: subscribe then publish, two tokens on one page, a revoke while disconnected and a
  reconnect pinned to today's presence behaviour (replaced in S4-ii by `subscription-ordered-reconnect`), and the
  same-context successor; the local lane is the evidence, and no hosted manifest carries the cells. The lane's control-run waits read through one `readControlRunUntil` over the
  shared `readUntil` (`packages/shared/resilience/timing/read-until.ts`): an absolute deadline on the injected timers, the
  caller's interval, and a typed `timed-out` outcome instead of a throw.

### Release 10, Slice 3 design (2026-11-03)

Designed in the Slice 3 design proposal from three read-only surveys of `main` at `5b1c4fcf6` (the RTC data path;
identity and authority; the harness and its proof gaps); the decisions are D512 to D523, under the maintainer's
rulings S3-R1–S3-R12 of 2026-11-03, each taken on its recommended option. Slice 3 lands as two pull requests (D523):
S3-i, the authenticated original publisher for granted room multicasts without a receipt, and S3-ii, the
`not-subscribed` receipt class, receipted granted sends, repair and fallback under role churn, and the relay-only
and four-role families over `rtc`. S3-ii's planning rulings PL1–PL28 are listed in its pull request; PL9–PL25,
PL27 and PL28 are provisional for the maintainer. The proposal is deleted with S3-ii's close: it is in git history
at `105f5392b` (#776), and its last tracked version, `5eeea2ea6` on PR #777, corrects S3-R3's sketch first:
`payload.resource` is signed directly, not through a SHA-256 of its bytes (D514).

- **The signature and its key (D512–D514, PL27, PL28).** A detached ECDSA P-256 signature over the domain-tagged,
  positional canonical JSON of the envelope's signed fields, `proof` an optional v4 section, signed once at RTC
  carrier admission and never re-signed. One key pair per session in the browser's IndexedDB, its public half on
  the session's presence row and snapshot, gone with the session; a key-only presence change replans no topology.
- **Admission at every hop (D515–D517).** Each relay and receiver judges a granted frame against its own readable
  room snapshot, at least as new as the frame; a failure drops `unauthorized` with no NACK, an unknown key or newer
  authority `not-yet-in-sync` after one refresh. Relays need membership only; delivery needs `subscribe` and an
  active token. A topic is granted at a page by its channel's declaration or its cached snapshot's grants.
- **The audience and the receipt (D518).** The origin freezes the grant-narrowed audience before it signs; a frozen
  recipient that may not deliver forwards, answers `not-subscribed` for itself, and relays carry that answer to the
  origin per recipient, where the receipt records it outside the audience. A WS copy after such an answer
  confirms nobody, and the WS receipt records it outside too.
- **Repair and fallback under churn (D519).** The origin re-checks its own `publish` before every repair, re-plan
  and dequeue, and a revoke ends the handle `rejected` `no-publish-grant`; a responder repairs only toward a frozen
  recipient still holding `subscribe`. Receipts stay unsigned, and payload bytes are not confidential from relays
  (D520).
- **The proof (D521).** Units, the relay fixture and eight `granted-rtc` cells on the local lane, the relay-only
  cell on a path whose middle the run draws, and the four-role family over `ws`, `rtc` and
  `rtc-with-ws-fallback` with the outside audience in its count identity.

### Release 11, Slice 4 design (2026-11-05)

Slice 4 was chosen from a candidate survey of the addendum's later outcomes: ordered subscription entry,
since every later ordered or history outcome needs a start-position contract. It was designed in the Slice 4 design
proposal, deleted with S4-ii and kept in git history, from read-only surveys of
the ordering tracks and repair, the server's subscription rows and WS path, and the harness, at `c673b4997`; the
decisions are D524 to D537, under the rulings S4-R1–S4-R14, each taken on its recommended option and provisional for
the maintainer. Slice 4 landed as two pull requests (D537): S4-i, the position record, both producers, the receiver
rules, browser minting, `before-entry` and the outside class on WS, and two four-role cells; S4-ii, the reopened
socket's presence (D506), relay re-origination of gap NACKs, the reconnect and relay cells, the restart proof and the
ordering counters.

- **The record (D524, D525).** The authority that finalizes a copy's audience keeps, per track and recipient, the
  last sequence it sent, beside the ordering head in its admission store, and states it on the copy as
  `ordering.priorSeqByRecipient`, listing only recipients whose prior is below `seq − 1`. The RTC origin records and
  signs it in its first admission; the WS server records at the first dequeue of a row its outbound admitted and
  stamps each copy with its recipient's own entry and no proof. Rows a producer writes straight to the outbox record
  nothing in S4-i.
- **The receiver (D526–D528).** Live from entry, no history: a recipient enters a recorded track at its first copy,
  delivers a copy whose record meets its position as `omitted`, asks a gap only up to a prior ahead of it, and
  witnesses a frozen copy it may not deliver; a relay observes nothing and forwards. The `ordering-position`
  diagnostic states each entry, omission, witness and `before-entry`.
- **Minting (D529).** A browser room send that names its ordering key without `seq` is sequenced by its outbound on
  the durable lane, from one head per track both carriers of a session share; a stated `seq` at or below the head is
  refused `unsupported`, and a reload continues the track. A sequence the WS leg sends the room moves the track's
  room-wide sent position beside the head, so the RTC origin's record never declares it an omission; a recipient the
  WS server left out of that send stalls until resync or expiry instead (D525), which S4-ii narrows to three residual
  windows.
- **Repair and receipts (D530, D532).** A recorded frozen copy below a recipient's position answers `before-entry`,
  which relays carry and the origin records outside the audience; WS copies carry no frozen audience, so over `ws`
  the server's skip does that work: the WS server sends nothing below a recorded position and, on a relayed
  browser-origin row with a logical receipt, records a session its dequeue re-check dropped, or a skipped recipient,
  outside the receipt's audience instead of unconfirmed; the server's own publications record no outside class.
- **Scope and proof (D533, D535, D536).** One mechanism for granted and `members` topics on RTC and for the WS
  outbound's admitted rows; generic pieces in `packages/shared`. Units, the relay and WS server fixtures, and the
  cells `subscription-ordered-entry` and `subscription-ordered-omission` over `ws`, `rtc` and `rtc-with-ws-fallback`
  on the local lane; `admittedAtGroupRevision` is deleted.
- **S4-ii (D531, D534, D525).** Decided under the rulings S4ii-R1–S4ii-R10, provisional for the maintainer: the
  server refuses a presence connect naming a dead connection generation `stale-generation` beside #785's restore of
  the selected room's presence, so a reconnect reads as an omission; relays re-originate a waited child's gap NACK
  toward the origin; a minted sequence continues across a reopened store; `readUsage().ordering` counts the position
  events; and the WS leg's `admitted` receipt narrows D525's stall to three residual windows, as the addendum's "As
  applied (S4-ii)" under Slice 4 states.

### Release 12, Slice 5 design (2026-11-07)

Slice 5 was chosen by the maintainer from a candidate survey of the addendum's later outcomes (S5-C0): positions for
the rows a producer writes straight to the WS outbox, leaving cross-instance positions and the fallback stall windows
out. It was designed in the Slice 5 design proposal, deleted with S5-i and kept in git history, from read-only surveys
of the producer rows, the WS server's ordering owner and the harness, at `13d783203`; the decisions are D538 to D550,
under the rulings S5-R1–S5-R13, each taken on its recommended option: eight by the maintainer, and five builder calls
open to the maintainer's override (D549). Slice 5 landed as one pull request, S5-i.

- **The index (D538–D542).** Every `WS_OUTBOX` row whose message names `ordering.seq` (Relic's round transitions and
  client-state principal events) is written with its `(track, seq)` index row, the `ordering-message` key the WS
  outbound admission already reads, in the producer's own AppInbox transaction and the outbox insert's own statement.
  The shared outbox pair computes, re-derives and writes it; a live index row under the key rolls the transaction
  back. The namespace is resolved once in composition from the WS runtime name.
- **The record (D543).** A producer row records at its first dequeue as a row the WS outbound admitted does, under its
  own sender version, so a mid-round Relic joiner enters at `seq 2` and a browser's first client-state event at
  `snapshotVersion` enters instead of reading a gap from 1.
- **The wait and its end (D544, D546).** A tracked row that has not recorded lists its track's index and holds on the
  nearest pending predecessor outside its batch, so a sequence nobody wrote and an expired predecessor hold nothing; a
  row whose dequeue ends terminally without recording clears its index row and releases its successors. The wait, the
  sent-position read and the outside writes move into the WS server's track-order owner.
- **The outside class (D545).** A recipient the server skipped or dropped on its own row is recorded outside its own
  pending receipt through one fenced commit, so a retry targets only the unconfirmed recipients.
- **Proof and gates (D547, D548).** Units, the WS server fixture's producer-row path, the Postgres-backed Relic
  publication unit and the api-v1 outside-class pin are blocking; the `server-ordered-entry` cell over `ws` is observed
  evidence. The addendum's "As applied (S5-i)" under Slice 5 states the limits.

### Release 13, Slice 6 design (2026-11-08)

Slice 6 was chosen by the maintainer from a candidate survey of the addendum's later outcomes (S6-C0): granted
unicast, fixed-list and room principal broadcast over RTC (1a-i), leaving signed receipts (1a-ii), an encrypted
publication (1b) and native publication-key custody (1c) out, with the postponed S5-i state-write comparison (6a) run
first. It was designed in the Slice 6 design proposal, now deleted (git history is the archive), from read-only
surveys of the granted carrier, the browser routing, the harness and the outbound riders, at `f175bd1a6`; the
decisions are D551 to D562, under the rulings S6-R1–S6-R12, each taken on its recommended option except S6-R8, S6-R9
and S6-R11, ruled (b): eight by the maintainer, and four builder calls open to the maintainer's override. Slice 6
lands as two pull requests (D561): S6-i, the RTC shapes, two outbound riders and the documents, and S6-ii, one writer
for the provenance sidecar, the batched CRDT, presence-summary and topology outbox loops and the shared PGlite
statement recorder.

- **The shapes (D551, D552).** A granted fixed list, room principal broadcast and room unicast ride RTC under `rtc`
  and `rtc-with-ws-fallback`; a unicast is translated into the one-entry listed room broadcast of its room and frozen
  as a signed multicast of one, so receivers, relays, the proof and the comparison readers do not change. An
  exclusions-only room broadcast stays refused `unsupported`, and peer sends stay unordered.
- **The audience (D553).** A named non-holder is frozen out silently, one rule for every shape; an audience frozen to
  nobody owns no children, so a `receiver` send completes a zero-recipient receipt and an `ack: 'none'` one falls back
  on `no-route`.
- **The room limit and the gates (D554, D555, D556, D557).** The granted leg judges the 256-entry bound right after
  its freeze, so a fallback takes over the sender's targets; one shape predicate in the carrier replaces the dispatch
  and facade copies; `ws-then-rtc` keeps granted messages on WS.
- **Proof, riders and gates (D558, D559, D560).** Units, the signing tests, the relay fixture and the granted-channel
  pins are blocking; five `granted-rtc` cells over `rtc` are observed evidence on the local lane, through a harness
  audience of lane roles or principal ids. The `track-index-end` outbound diagnostic and `readOrderingMessageId` ride
  S6-i; the provenance writer, the batched CRDT, presence-summary and topology outbox loops and the PGlite statement
  recorder are S6-ii. The addendum's "As applied (S6-i)" under Slice 6 states the limits.

**The second pull request (D563–D567).** S6-ii folded the producer proof into the shared outbox insert: the proof is
the row's second sidecar row, derived in compute from the producer's facts, checked by `validateWsOutboxInsert`
outside the write, and written in the one `sidecars` CTE beside the track index. One conflict rule holds for every
proof, absent-or-expired, with Relic aligned. Auth logout, client state, CRDT, the presence summary, topology and
Relic lost their raw writers, and the connect its proof effect; on those six producer paths and the connect batch one
proof statement per proved row is folded, while the ~10 view-invalidation producers keep their guarded batch, and the
CRDT, presence-summary and topology commits went from 2N statements to 1. The shared raw-PGlite recorder
`recordPGliteStatements` replaced four private copies. The medium-scale gate passed in CI on every head, and the
state-write measurement of S6-ii's own is guidance, reported in the pull request.

### Release 14, Slice 7 design (2026-11-09)

Slice 7 was chosen by the maintainer from a candidate survey of the addendum's later outcomes (S7-C0): cross-instance
positions and the outside class (2c-ii), with the three-fence residual, `buffered-track-drains` over `ws`, the
admin-audience append and a `vi`-free recorder riding and the 6b measurement first, leaving signed receipts (1a-ii),
an encrypted publication (1b), native publication-key custody (1c) and the fallback stall windows (2c-iii) out. The
surveys corrected its premise: the record gap was real for granted rows only and the receipt gap for every receipted
server row, single-instance included. The maintainer re-shaped it (S7-C0b): no merge write; the durable record and
judgement at the dequeue, the bridge reporting its send-time drops, a typed diagnostic for three lost fences and a new
ordering cluster proof. It was designed in the Slice 7 design proposal, now deleted (git history is the archive), from
the candidates survey and three read-only surveys of the cluster path, the track-order owner and its store, and the
probe, riders and documents, at `2279d4f3b`; the decisions are D568 to D580, under the rulings S7-R1–S7-R11, each
taken on its recommended option (a): six by the maintainer, and five builder calls open to the maintainer's override;
D579 and D580 follow the maintainer's rulings S7ii-R1 and S7ii-R2 during S7-ii.
Slice 7 lands as two pull requests (D576): S7-i, the probe, the mechanism, the proof and the documents, server-only,
and S7-ii, the riders.

- **Who is judged (D568).** Every captured row is judged from durable presence at the dequeue and the retry; a session
  with a live generation anywhere is recorded and expected, one with none is dropped and recorded outside (co-members
  on principal rows kept, D568); the local-socket filter applies only at send.
- **Send-time drops (D569).** The bridge reports `captured − eligible` beside the skips; a dequeue or retry drop is
  judged durably, a send-time drop open-here, and a session live nowhere waits for the retry.
- **Three lost fences (D570).** One typed `outside-audience-commit` diagnostic, no console line; the retry re-judges.
- **6b (D571).** A Postgres probe of the tracked dequeue, counts primary, before and after; D544's wording corrected.
- **The proof (D572).** A blocking ordering cluster proof beside view push, plus the unit pins.
- **`buffered-track-drains` over ws (D573).** A per-gap attempt identity; as applied, it holds per requester for the
  message's repairable lifetime, and the `ws` leg is observed locally, with the promotion wait `rtc`-only.
- **The admin-audience append (D574).** Refused at decode; as applied, a `TypeError` classed
  `app-inbox-malformed-command`.
- **The recorder (D575).** A `vi`-free recorder both runtimes import; as applied, under `apps/api-v1/test/db/` with a
  caller-owned `restore()`.
- **The landing (D576).** Two pull requests, S7-i server-only, S7-ii the riders.
- **The documents (D577).** "As applied" corrections on D524, D532, D544 and D545, not rewrites; the proposal deleted.
- **The gates (D578).** Medium-scale by path; no state-write measurement; no bundle figure in S7-i.
- **The `repair-exhausted` cell (D579).** A three-agent cell: the second receiver's report of the held gap finds the
  budget spent.
- **The cell's carriers (D580).** `rtc` and `rtc-with-ws-fallback` only; over `ws` the server is the gap's one
  requester, a limit, and a per-recipient server report a carry.

**As applied (S7-i).** The WS server's re-check is two filters, `durable` judging the dequeue and the retry and `local`
every send; api-v1's `filterDurablyLiveWsSessionIds` reads a room's live generations from its publication authority
and a principal's stored and live session rows through `readPrincipalSessions`, keeping co-member sessions it cannot
judge. `writeOutsideAudience` takes `'durable'` or `'open-here'`, the bridge reports its send-time drops, a judged
dequeue that reaches no socket here sends to nobody here (`audienceJudgedAtSend`), and three lost fences are one
diagnostic. The 6b counts are identical on the front before and after; the probe measures the authority batch read the
durable re-check adds (one statement), a room row gains at least two (the snapshot read and the batch), and the
principal path is unmeasured. The
ordering cluster proof proves the record and entry half on both tracks and the outside judgement on the
receipt-retry path, since holding the dequeuer would hold every AppInbox mutation. The addendum's "As applied (S7-i)"
under Slice 7 states the limits.

**As applied (S7-ii).** A repair hint's paged sequences are charged once per gap:
`toALOutboundRepairGapAttemptIdentity` names the requester, track, sequence and logical recipient, and the fallback
and `ack-timeout` paths keep the hint's identity. Completed send rows are retained until the message expires, so one
requester's later reports of a gap charge nothing for the message's repairable lifetime, and exhaustion is another
identity's finding: the WS server hop or another receiver. `buffered-track-drains` declares both carriers; its `ws`
leg is observed locally over `ws` (the full-scope lane; the gate's observation job runs the smoke scope), its earlier
red was the receiver's promotion wait, which only the RTC receiver can satisfy, and that wait is now `rtc`-only. The
`repair-exhausted` cell is a three-agent cell over the RTC carriers (D579, D580), observation only. The CRDT codec
refuses an admin-audience `append` at decode, and the `vi`-free `recordPGliteStatements` under `apps/api-v1/test/db/`
serves both runtimes. `browser/rallar.ts` measured 298.0 KiB and its budget was raised to 299 KiB; the headless agent
measured 394.516 KiB under 395. The addendum's "As applied (S7-ii)" under Slice 7 states the limits.

## Conformance lane

One scenario catalog, run over both carriers, is the acceptance authority for every release. A
scenario is proven only when its assertion establishes the guarantee. Operations and recipe schema
live in `rallar-bb-test`; scenario recipes live in the `alm-conformance` family beside the API
recipes; server-only paths use API recipes in the api-v1 Postgres profile.

Rules baked in from past runs: distinct identities per recipe because `runId` is shared per profile;
per-issue command ids because the control server replays a reissued id as success; pinned ports per
session; readiness only after activation and plans only after presence settles; scenario artifacts
named in the PR body as evidence.

Each PR adds its family: F1 baseline; S1 lifecycle matrix over every settlement and state; S2
identity and receipts with three peers, relay changes, join and leave, lost ACK, duplicate arrival
across carriers, both fallback orders; S3 volatile counters, fallback within the deadline, budgets;
P1 the storage figures per tier; I2a takeover, `storage-unavailable` and recovery outcomes; I2b
checkpoint recovery, lag and flush on hide; R1 and R2 arbitration and fencing; A1 and A2 audiences,
leader, claims; V1 scale; I1a reply correlation. The
[QoS plan's evidence table](alm-qos-product-plan.md#9-test-and-evidence-plan) maps each release 4
requirement to its layer. Its storage fault port is a black-box capability, never product
behaviour.

**Observation status (2026-09-11, maintainer decision).** The lane runs as the Release Gate's non-blocking observation job with its budgets unchanged (`CONNECT_READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS` 30 s, the receiver window from the 18 s scenario deadline, a 10 s non-expiring send). The hosted runner's IndexedDB speed varies by about two between runs, and the rtc cell passes below roughly 30 ms per operation and fails above 35, so every artifact carries a runner-regime summary (F2 Task 14) and a red counts as a regression only against a green baseline of the same regime. **Follow-up slice, F2b — the inbound owner on slow storage:** in the slow regime the receiver's inbound drain runs 5–14 s per batch (0.3–1.1 s otherwise), the pending share of inbound admissions rises to 63–65 % on the RTC cells, and a ws message admitted as pending is committed but not dispatched before its window closes; the section "Release 3, F2b" carries the treatment, and the lane returns to `test:ci` only on its evidence. On merged `main` (`f8db93762`) every cell ran in the slow regime and all three failed with that signature. F2b measured on the runner (`80d017d24`, 2026-09-11): a 48–55 ms per operation regime, the slowest yet and
one without a same-regime green baseline; inbound batch medians of 5–14 s against outbound 1.3–2.4 s, so
F2b's acceptance is not met there, while the lane passes 3 of 3 locally at 7–13 ms per operation. The phase
split F2b added attributes the batches to the claims' own work and their releases, fed by a 70–77 % pending
share: the inbound fence re-reads the whole decision surface, so every concurrent control or ACK commit
conflicts the data admission in flight. Narrowing that fence and batching releases are admission-design
changes for the next slice, the maintainer's call.
Since S3a (R-S3a-15, R-S3a-16) the per-operation regime spans the cell's durable (IndexedDB) send commits,
and the page regime decides a cell in which no durable send ran.

## Storage, cutover, reset, and rollback

- **Browser.** One ALM-owned database per application scope and origin, `rallar-al-runtime:${applicationId}:${workspaceId}`, with a schema identity (D120).
  - **Schema mismatch.** Since #652 an open whose stores or schema identity differ is refused with
    `ALStorageSchemaMismatchError` and the database is kept as it is
    (`packages/shared/alm/open-indexed-db-admission-database.ts`); D3's delete-on-mismatch is a
    follow-up in `plans/backlog.md`. An observed recreation by another context reaches the `storage`
    diagnostics port as a `reset` event, which the black-box harness emits as
    `rallar.browser.alm.storage_reset`.
  - **Stores.** Two stores, admission and work, with bounded indexes.
  - **Durability.** Durability is a channel property, and each channel is routed to exactly one
    backend.
  - **Tabs.** Cross-tab commit locking stays on Web Locks. The per-session durable owner (I2a) is
    a second lock name on the same BrowserLocks port: non-owners commit but run no durable work
    tasks, another tab takes over on release, and a per-scope-and-session BroadcastChannel carries
    the commit wake and the owner's settlement relay (D120–D123).
  - **Storage failures.** Quota, eviction, a failed open, a closed connection and missing storage are
    typed `storage-unavailable` outcomes (I2a): an admission verdict read as
    state `failed`, or under `onStorageUnavailable: 'volatile'` a volatile admission with a
    `durabilityDowngrade` note. None of them falls back to memory silently; the `storage` port
    reports reset, recovery, health and persist events (D120–D123).
  - **Checkpoints and scope.** `local-checkpoint` (I2b) checkpoints into the same database. In I2a
    each scope gets its own database, `rallar-al-runtime:${applicationId}:${workspaceId}`, with keys
    session-scoped inside; only the name takes the scope, so the schema id is unchanged, and the
    legacy `ar-eye-hunter-al-runtime` is left to the browser's eviction (D120–D123).
- **Server.** PostgreSQL ResourceInbox is the only durable work owner. Schema changes are additive
  Prisma migrations; an applied migration is never edited. Per-recipient delivery facts for durable
  notifications live in the existing results tables under AppInbox until the message deadline.
  Broadcast ACKs route to the origin connection; for durable channels they are retained as receipt
  facts until the deadline when the origin is offline.
- **Cutover.** F2, S1, S2, and R2 are incompatible. Each lands contracts, consumers, examples,
  harness, and recipes together, deletes the old path, and lists in the PR body what pending ALM
  work is discarded. Web and API deploy together from `main`.
- **Rollback.** Revert the merge commit. A browser database written under another schema id is
  refused, not reset (see "Schema mismatch"); server migrations are
  additive; a mismatched envelope version is a typed rejection visible in diagnostics.
- **Measurement.** Every cutover PR records the storage snapshot per message state for the standard
  workload (eight updates, three recipients, 128 B, 4 KiB, and 64 KiB payloads) from the lane's
  counters and compares it with the previous PR. A regression needs a stated reason. Every ALM PR
  also reports the per-tier storage budgets beside its bundle figures (D87).

## Governance and delivery rules

- **Legacy.** Every affected item ends `removed` or `resolved`. No compatibility fallback, no
  browser data migration, no envelope version window.
- **Libraries.** Decision D8.
- **Bundle.** `rallar-messages.ts` has its own budget. The aggregate facade keeps the maintainer
  ruling: a crossed budget is raised to the next whole KiB with the measured figure recorded. Both
  figures appear in every PR body.
- **Checker.** After F2 no new `file.cognitive-load` pin on an ALM file. A `boundary.unknown` waiver
  only for a genuine `decodeXxx(value: unknown): Either` boundary. Every disposition entry carries
  its own comment. The exception registry is used only for its three real cases.
- **Red-head prevention.** Every commit keeps `test:unit`, the three Deno checks, and `dprint check`
  green; tests change in the same commit as the production change; the PR body names the commit each
  figure was measured on; the Branch Release Gate is green before review is requested;
  `pr:delivery status` decides the next action; `ready` and auto-merge are not used.
- **PR shape.** Goal, Changes, Acceptance, Validation, Risk and rollback, Follow-up. Acceptance names
  the conformance scenarios and API recipes; Validation names their artifacts. One active slice at a
  time from merged `main`.
- **Tests.** Semantic tests through real owners with narrow clock and transport fakes. An obsolete
  coupled test is rewritten in the same PR. `deno task check` for api-v1 runs whenever a shared type
  changes.
- **Navigation maps.** The inbound and outbound READMEs are updated in every PR that changes their
  owners and never claim behavior the code does not have.

## Validation and performance

Required layers, per PR: focused semantic tests through real owners; storage parity across memory,
IndexedDB, and real PostgreSQL where affected; the conformance family over both carriers; the
affected browser workflow; package validation (typechecks, public API snapshots, bundle boundaries,
`deno task check` for api-v1, repo style); and the reuse inspection required by D8.

```sh
npx vitest run packages/tests/shared/alm packages/tests/shared-web/al-runtime packages/tests/shared-server/al-runtime
npx tsc -p packages/shared/tsconfig.json --noEmit
npm --workspace @ar-eye-hunter/shared-web run typecheck
npm --workspace @ar-eye-hunter/shared-server run typecheck
cd apps/api-v1 && deno task check
npm --workspace @ar-eye-hunter/shared-web run check:browser-bundles
npm run check:repo-style:changed -- origin/main HEAD
npm run test:full-stack:memory
npm run test:api-v1:black-box:postgres
npm run test:api-v1:black-box:postgres:medium-scale
```

The medium-scale and state-write gates apply to every PR that changes an authoritative mutation
path or concurrency domain, with unchanged workloads and thresholds. ALM measurements extend the
existing `messages.rtc` workload with AL-owned transactions, visited and decoded rows, bytes, work
age, retries, repairs, terminal counts, and receipt latency, recorded as p50, p95, and p99 with
environment, configuration, sample count, and failures. Serialized readback bytes are layout
evidence, not physical allocation or latency. Artifacts live under `tmp/perf/` locally and as CI
artifacts in the lanes.

**Storage budgets (D87).** The operation-count pins are the per-tier storage budgets:
`al-indexeddb-operation-counts.test.ts`, `al-indexeddb-transaction-ledger.test.ts`,
`al-storage-snapshot.test.ts` and `indexeddb-queuebox-operation-counts.test.ts`. They are named
interaction assertions whose count is the requirement. The number of transactions on a warm durable
send's chain from `enqueueIfAbsent` to the carrier send is a budget too (D109). A pin may only fall. A rise needs a stated reason in the PR body, which reports the
figures beside the bundle figures. Latency per tier is judged under the runner-regime rule. Storage
failures are exercised through the black-box storage fault port, never through a product switch.
The [QoS plan](alm-qos-product-plan.md#91-layers) names the layer each requirement lands in.
